tagline: Reads a fixed 4K junction camera, reports every traffic event as a time segment with a class, and raises an alarm when two road users are about to collide.

approach.summary: One pass over the video: a COCO-pretrained YOLO11s detector with ByteTrack tracks vehicles and pedestrians, the traffic light is read from its lit section, and hand-written rules on the trajectories and a hand-drawn scene layout produce the events. The scene layout is mapped to every recording by a homography, because the 'fixed' camera moves between recordings. Part B is a separate causal pass: YOLO11n + ByteTrack and a closest-approach / required-deceleration risk for every pair of road users.

pipeline.name: Video
pipeline.detail: 4K H.264 at 29.97 fps, decoded once in a reader thread; every 3rd frame (10 Hz) goes to the detector, only the strip above the scene zones (top 4 %, trees) is cropped.

pipeline.name: Scene alignment
pipeline.detail: CLAHE + SIFT on the static background against day, sunset and dusk reference frames, RANSAC homography, median over three frames of the clip; zones drawn once are mapped to this recording.

pipeline.name: Detection + tracking
pipeline.detail: YOLO11s (COCO weights, fp16, 1280 px input) finds cars, buses, trucks, motorcycles, bicycles and people; ByteTrack links them into tracks; track fragments are stitched.

pipeline.name: Traffic light
pipeline.detail: Which of the three sections is lit (not colour counts); frames where a closer vehicle covers the signal are skipped; green to red without yellow must hold 3 s.

pipeline.name: Event rules
pipeline.detail: Per-class rules on tracks, zones and the signal state: congestion, stopped_vehicle, jaywalking, red_light, stop_line, illegal_turn; segments merged and cleaned per class.

pipeline.name: Accident risk (Part B)
pipeline.detail: Causal: YOLO11n + ByteTrack on every 2nd frame in a worker thread; for every pair, the closest approach and the deceleration still needed to avoid contact; median over 0.6 s.

pipeline.name: Output
pipeline.detail: [[start_sec, end_sec, label], ...] per video and a risk score per frame, in the harness format.

models.name: YOLO11s (Ultralytics)
models.role: Part A detector: vehicles and pedestrians, COCO-pretrained, not fine-tuned
models.why: Accurate enough on far, small objects at 1280 px and fast enough to leave half of the 3× budget; COCO already has every class we need, and without labels for this camera there is nothing to fine-tune on.

models.name: YOLO11n (Ultralytics)
models.why: Part B runs frame by frame inside the harness; the nano model keeps it cheap while the risk only needs rough positions and speeds.

models.name: ByteTrack (Ultralytics implementation)
models.why: Keeps low-confidence detections to bridge occlusions (a bus passing a moped) without an appearance model, so it adds almost no time.

models.name: SIFT (OpenCV)
models.role: features for aligning the scene zones to each recording
models.why: Scale- and rotation-invariant; with CLAHE it still finds hundreds of matches at sunset and dusk, where ORB found 16–21.

datasets.name: COCO 2017
datasets.use: Pre-training of the YOLO11 weights by Ultralytics (not used by us directly)

datasets.name: The four sample videos
datasets.use: Scene zones, thresholds and visual checks; no training

learned: Object detection (YOLO11s / YOLO11n, COCO weights, not fine-tuned)
rule_based: All event rules and segment post-processing

class_rules.label: congestion
class_rules.rule: At least 4 cars standing together in the main-road queue that keep standing through 15 s or more of green (a normal red-light queue clears on green), or a dense block of cars standing on the junction for 40 s or more (longer than one signal phase).

class_rules.label: stopped_vehicle
class_rules.rule: A vehicle stationary on the carriageway for 10 s or more that is not packed in a queue (2 or more other stopped cars within 1.5 box diagonals for half of its stop) and not waiting at the signal; on the junction itself any lone stop counts.

class_rules.label: jaywalking
class_rules.rule: A pedestrian's ground point on the carriageway outside the crossings and the pedestrian islands for 1 s or more; people whose box sits inside a vehicle box (riders, passengers) are ignored.

class_rules.label: red_light
class_rules.rule: A vehicle enters the stop-line zone on red and reaches the far crossing while the signal is still red; a vehicle that stops past the line and drives on only when it turns green is stop_line instead.

class_rules.label: stop_line
class_rules.rule: A vehicle stops for 1.5 s or more on red past the stop line: on the band before the far zebra or on the zebra itself, within the lanes of the main-road queue. The segment ends when the signal turns green. Not reported for vehicles that then enter the junction on red (those are red_light).

class_rules.label: illegal_turn
class_rules.rule: The forbidden route of this junction: from the main-road queue deep into the junction, a U-shaped turn at the apex and out through the lower end of the near crossing within 3 s.

approach.runtime: On the four sample videos (RTX 5050 laptop, 8 CPU cores): 1.4-1.9x the video duration for Part A + Part B together, 46-63 % of the 3x budget; the spread comes from load on the machine, not from the clips. Decoding 4K dominates; the detector is cheap. Time guards raise the frame stride if a slower machine would miss the budget, instead of losing the whole video.
approach.rules_why: There are no labels for this camera, so every event is an explicit rule on tracks, zones and the signal state. Each rule can be checked by watching the rendered video, and each threshold is stated on this page.

report.built: A detector + tracker + rules system for one fixed junction camera. Everything that depends on the scene (zones, the traffic light, the forbidden turn) is drawn once and mapped to every recording by a homography, so camera shifts between recordings do not break it. Six classes are submitted; eight more have rules but stay off until they can be checked, because a predicted class that is absent from the test set costs F1 = 0. Part B is a causal pairwise collision-risk score calibrated to almost never alarm on normal traffic. A live demo runs the same code on uploaded clips.
worked: Aligning the scene by homography with a bank of day, sunset and dusk references: 60/60 synthetic camera shifts within 1 px, including tilts that a shift + rotation model missed by up to 262 px.
Reading the traffic light by which section is lit, with occlusion handling: unknown dropped from 36-100 % to 0-2 % of frames in the day clips.
Required deceleration instead of plain time-to-collision for the risk: risk of 0.5 or more on 57-71 % of frames with the first version, one alarm of 0.5 s in 18 min in the submitted run.
Letting ByteTrack see low-confidence detections (conf 0.1): median track length 7.5 s to 9.7 s.
Overlapping decoding with inference in both parts: 2.2x to 1.4-1.9x of the video duration.

Pairing only vehicles at a similar depth: two cars whose boxes differ in size by more than 2.2x are metres apart on the ground; this removed the 'near car heads for a car far down the road' false alarm.

stop_line by the task definition: a stop on red anywhere past the line (the band before the zebra or the zebra itself, in the lanes of the queue); vehicles that waited there and left on green are no longer counted as red_light.

Splitting tracks that switch between person and vehicle (ByteTrack hands a pedestrian's id to the car that covers it) and treating fast, squat 'people' on the road as scooter riders whose scooter the detector missed: 8 false jaywalking events removed on the samples.

Cropping only the strip above the scene zones (4 % instead of 18 %): the far lanes and the bus stop are analysed now; six stops at the far kerb that were invisible before are detected, at no measurable runtime cost.
did_not_work: Part B is too cautious: on synthetic crashes it raises the alarm for 40 % of them and only ~0.1 s before contact, and it misses rear-end crashes at city speed. Every looser variant we tried catches more crashes (up to 93 %) but also fires 15-43 times on 18 minutes of normal traffic (measured before the depth check below), because in image space a dense queue looks like a crash; with accidents rare, those false alarms cost more alarm-F1 than the extra hits bring. The samples contain no accidents, so recall is only measured on synthetic scenarios.

Distances in image space for Part B: perspective squeezes gaps, so a pedestrian on an island next to a passing car looks like a contact (the one false alarm on the samples), and close following in slow traffic scores up to 0.48.

Motorcycles and mopeds: the COCO-trained YOLO11 often misses them on this camera, especially far away or next to cars and buses, so their boxes flicker or vanish for a few frames. The track then breaks, and a red-light or illegal-turn run by a two-wheeler can be missed. Lowering the tracker threshold to conf 0.1 helped (one courier moped: 43 → 61 of 80 frames covered) but did not solve it.
'Any turn inside a polygon' for illegal_turn: it flagged legal manoeuvres around trucks and missed the real U-turns, which happen below the polygon and turn by more than 150 degrees.
A plain '4 cars standing' congestion rule: every red phase became congestion.
Our own labels of the samples are not finished, so there is no dev-set F1 yet; thresholds were set by watching the rendered videos.
next: Finish labelling the samples and tune thresholds per class against evaluate.py.

Project tracks to the ground plane: metric gaps and speeds would separate a queue from a crash, which image-space distances cannot (see the Part B ablation). We tried a single-view calibration from this frame (vanishing points of lane lines and of the stop line and zebra) and it does not hold: the road is not straight and the junction is skewed, the lane-line vanishing point moves by hundreds of pixels between line subsets and the orthogonality constraint has no solution. It needs 4-6 surveyed points on the asphalt (tape measure or a cadastral map).
Validate the experimental classes (wrong_way, failure_to_yield, solid_line_crossing, accident, near_miss) and switch on the ones that pass.
Fine-tune the detector on this camera view (far, small objects; motorcycles, mopeds and scooters, which YOLO11 misses most).
